details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:440-448 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: `included += 1` runs even when `_overflow_fallback_lines()` returns no output.
  WHY: All reviewers that flagged it agree this creates a phantom marker-only count in the summary when `semble_fallback="off"`; none disputed the control flow.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:228-237, 518 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: `--semble-fallback read` is accepted by the CLI but has no distinct implementation.
  WHY: The parser advertises `read`, but `_overflow_fallback_lines()` only special-cases `off`, so `read` silently falls through to legacy marker behavior.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:424-441 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: Semble output is added to `used_bytes` without checking it against `max_bytes`.
  WHY: A large Semble response can push the targeted-context block past the configured budget because the added bytes bypass the overflow check.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:903-914 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: `CLARIFICATION_ANSWERS_FILE` is read under `set -euo pipefail` without a fallback guard.
  WHY: Some reviewers treated this as a current bug, while others said the variable is initialized earlier in the same job and the current step ordering is safe; the highest reported severity is medium.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:155-171 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: `_sanitize_one_line` collapses structured query text into one line.
  WHY: Reviewers flagged that flattening section boundaries can degrade retrieval quality, though one reviewer treated the sanitization as deliberate.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:155-161 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: An explicit `--semble-bin` path that fails validation is dropped without a diagnostic.
  WHY: The helper falls back to PATH lookup or `None` silently, so operator misconfiguration is hard to distinguish from missing-binary cases.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:152-174 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: `_load_semble_query_text` reads the full file before truncating to the cap.
  WHY: Oversized query files can consume unnecessary memory before the 4000-character limit is applied.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:190-206 | severity=low | confidence=1
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The Semble subprocess lacks process-group isolation hardening.
  WHY: This was called out as defense-in-depth hardening only, not as a correctness bug.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:442-447 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: included += 1 executes even when no fallback marker is emitted.
  WHY: When `semble_fallback="off"`, `_overflow_fallback_lines()` can return `[]`, but `included` still increments and the summary reports a marker-only entry that was never written.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:228-237 (implementation), 518 (parser) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `--semble-fallback read` is accepted but not implemented.
  WHY: The parser allows `read`, but `_overflow_fallback_lines()` only distinguishes `off`, so `read` silently behaves like `marker`.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:438-441 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Semble retrieval body bytes are added to `used_bytes` without a `max_bytes` check.
  WHY: A large Semble response can push the context budget over the limit and affect later overflow decisions.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:171 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `_sanitize_one_line` flattens structured query text.
  WHY: Newlines and section boundaries are collapsed into one line, which can reduce retrieval quality.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:903-914 | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: `CLARIFICATION_ANSWERS_FILE` may be unset in the Semble query step.
  WHY: I traced the workflow and found the variable is set earlier in the same job, so this is not a current failure path.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:156-161 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `_resolve_semble_bin` lacks diagnostics when an explicit path is rejected.
  WHY: A non-file or non-executable `--semble-bin` returns `None` with no signal that the explicit configuration was ignored.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:164-174 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `_load_semble_query_text` reads the entire file before truncation.
  WHY: The query text is truncated later, but the initial `read_text()` still loads the full file into memory.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

  PROBLEM: `included += 1` runs unconditionally in the overflow/fallback branch.
  WHY: When `_overflow_fallback_lines()` returns `[]`, the summary count still increases even though nothing was emitted.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:518 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `--semble-fallback read` is advertised but falls through to marker behavior.
  WHY: The CLI exposes `read`, but `_overflow_fallback_lines()` only treats `off` specially.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:437-439 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The Semble body is appended to `used_bytes` without checking the budget.
  WHY: An oversized retrieval can push the targeted-context block beyond `max_bytes`.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:911 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `cat "${CLARIFICATION_ANSWERS_FILE}"` is used without a default guard.
  WHY: Under `set -euo pipefail`, an unset variable would abort the step instead of degrading gracefully.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:155 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `_sanitize_one_line()` collapses multi-section query documents.
  WHY: Whitespace normalization removes structure that may help retrieval.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:190-206 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The Semble subprocess could use process-group isolation.
  WHY: This is defense-in-depth hardening to reduce process-control leakage or orphaning.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:156-161 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: An explicit `--semble-bin` path failure is silently ignored.
  WHY: If validation fails, the code falls back to PATH lookup with no diagnostic.

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:447 (the `included += 1` after the fallback block) | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `included += 1` executes unconditionally in the overflow/fallback branch regardless of whether any output was actually produced.
  WHY: When `semble_fallback="off"` and Semble retrieval also yields nothing, `_overflow_fallback_lines()` returns `[]`, but the summary still counts a marker-only entry that was never written.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:517-518 (`parser.add_argument("--semble-fallback", choices=("marker", "read", "off"), default="marker")`) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The CLI parser advertises `read` as a valid `--semble-fallback` choice, but `_overflow_fallback_lines()` only special-cases `off`.
  WHY: Operators who set `--semble-fallback read` get the legacy overflow marker with no diagnostic or warning.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:424-430 (the Semble success branch inside the overflow block) | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The Semble response body is added to `used_bytes` without checking the remaining budget.
  WHY: A large retrieval can push the targeted-context block past `max_bytes`, bypassing the overflow guard that only runs before the Semble fetch.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:156-161 (`_resolve_semble_bin`) | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: An explicit `--semble-bin` path that fails validation is silently ignored.
  WHY: The caller gets no signal that the explicit binary path was rejected, so misconfiguration is hidden.

  WHY: I verified the variable is initialized earlier in the same job and the step ordering is safe, so this is not a current bug.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:190-206 |

  WHY: This was noted as a hardening observation only, not a correctness issue.
